english.notes:
Section 6 of the Violent Crime Reduction Act 2006 (Orders on conviction in criminal proceedings) was repealed on 20th October 2014. From that date, no new orders will be made under section 6, however, orders made before 20th October under that section, which are then breached, may still be prosecuted using this offence code.

(i) This is a breach and although section 11(4) of the Violent Crime Reduction Act 2006 provides that a local authority may bring proceedings, a breach is a criminal offence in the same way that a breach of an ASBO is a criminal offence. As such it enables a police officer to apply the necessity test under section 24 of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 to ascertain if the person in breach should be arrested. If the necessity test is not fulfilled the officer should report the person for summons. In any event, as it is a criminal offence and as detailed in the HO guidance, the CPS would prosecute.
(ii) Section 11(3) of the Violent Crime Reduction Act 2006 provides that if a person is convicted of this offence it is not open to the court by or before which he is convicted to make an order under subsection (1)(b) (conditional discharge) of section 12 of the Powers of Criminal Courts (Sentencing) Act 2000.
(iii) Section 11(6) of the Violent Crime Reduction Act 2006 makes a requirement for the provision of a copy of the original drinking banning order or interim order during breach proceedings.
(iv) Section 11(7) of the Violent Crime Reduction Act 2006 provides that if proceedings for this are brought in a youth court, section 47(2) of the Children and Young Persons Act 1933 has effect as if the persons entitled to be present for the purposes of those proceedings included one person authorised to be present by a relevant authority.
(v) Sections 11(8) and 11(9) of the Violent Crime Reduction Act 2006 provides for proceedings brought against a young person for this offence.
(vi) There appears to be no minimum age limit under the County Court.
(vii) These Orders can occur in the ways, on application to a Magistrates' Court under section 3, in the County Court under section 4 and in criminal proceedings under section 6.
(viii) See also H8711 for the wording re drinking banning orders.
